R Notebook

Picked >= 4 felt reports because it looked good, Hazel has said we need to have strong justification. She suggested comparing the standard deviation as the minimum number of felt reports are needed, and standard error for random effects.

Data Preparation

Reads the two datasets and joins the Vs30 data to the main dataset based on the nearest Vs30 data point.

library(arrow)
library(MASS)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaps)
library(lme4)


data <- read_parquet("data_processed/NZ_FR_IAR_final_dataset.parquet")

data <- data |>
  drop_na(
    Rhypo_km,
    mt_Mw,
    Vs30_raw,
    event_depth_km,
    publicid
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    calculated_median = {
      
      counts <- as.integer(c(
        felt_mmi_1_reports,
        felt_mmi_2_reports,
        felt_mmi_3_reports,
        felt_mmi_4_reports,
        felt_mmi_5_reports,
        felt_mmi_6_reports,
        felt_mmi_7_reports,
        felt_mmi_8_reports
      ))
      
      if (sum(counts) > 0) {
        median(rep(1:8, times = counts))
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    }
  ) |>
  ungroup()
View(data)


# filters the dataset to the decided upon report count
data_sd <- data |>
  filter(report_count >= 4)

Box-Cox Model

Trying out other predictors and applying best subset selection.

model_bc <- regsubsets(
  calculated_median ~ event_depth_km + Rhypo_km + Vs30_raw + mt_Mw + Rcentroid_km + catalogue_magnitude,
  data = data_sd,
  nvmax = 3
)

Checking Vs30 data as no model wants to use it

Uses a Box-Cox transformation to find the most suitable transformation of felt_mmi_median_cells for only Vs30.

bc <- boxcox(
  lm(calculated_median ~ mt_Mw + Rcentroid_km + catalogue_magnitude, data = data_sd)
)


best_lambda <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
best_lambda
[1] 2
model_lr <- lm(
  (I(calculated_median^2) ~ mt_Mw + Rcentroid_km + catalogue_magnitude),
  data = data_sd
  )

Best Subset Selection

Uses best subset selection to compare combinations of earthquake depth, hypocentral distance, moment magnitude and Vs30 for predicting the Median MMI.

model_lr_rss <- regsubsets(
  calculated_median ~ event_depth_km + Rhypo_km + Vs30_raw + mt_Mw + Rcentroid_km,
  data = data_sd,

)

Filtering Felt Reports

With the selected variables applies a Box-Cox analysis to determine the most suitable transformation for the filtered data.

model_lr_bc <- boxcox(
  lm(calculated_median ~ event_depth_km + Rhypo_km + Vs30_raw + mt_Mw, data = data_sd)
)


best_lambda <- model_lr_bc$x[which.max(model_lr_bc$y)]
best_lambda
[1] 2
model_lr_bc2 <- boxcox(
  lm(calculated_median ~ event_depth_km + Rcentroid_km + Vs30_raw + mt_Mw, data = data_sd)
)


best_lambda2 <- model_lr_bc2$x[which.max(model_lr_bc2$y)]
best_lambda2
[1] 2

Mixed-Effects Model

Fits a linear mixed-effects model with earthquake ID (publicid) as a random effect to account for multiple observations coming from the same earthquake. still very Work in progress

model_mem_1 <- lmer(
  log(calculated_median) ~ Rhypo_km + (1 | publicid), data = data_sd,
  REML = FALSE
